clue.text: Get the gun ready for shooting the bird

definitions.text: Get the gun ready for shooting
definitions.meaning: to raise the hammer of a firearm so it can fire
a male fowl, the farmyard rooster

explanation.surface: A hunter readies the gun to shoot down a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising a gun's hammer is the verb sense; a rooster is the noun sense of the same word.

clue.text: Brown seems to have been of international calibre

definitions.meaning: Lancelot Brown, the famous 18th-century English landscape gardener, had this nickname
calibre in the sense of ability or competence

explanation.surface: Someone named Brown appears to have been a world-class performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancelot 'Capability' Brown designed the grounds of many great English country houses.
explanation.definitionFit: The gardener's nickname, and a word meaning competence or ability, which is what calibre measures.

clue.text: Feature conscious crocks

parts.note: the chin is a feature of the face
aware means conscious, alert to

explanation.surface: A characteristic of someone conscious who is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crocks' looks like old wrecks of people, but it means earthenware pots and dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocks are pots and dishes, and porcelain tableware is a kind of such crockery.

clue.text: It is tiresome to be out of form at golf

parts.note: a player off form is said to be off
putting is the stroke on the green at golf

explanation.surface: It is wearying to play badly on the golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Something discouraging or unpleasant is tiresome, a close synonym.

clue.text: Cross about fighting, in the van

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the crossing word surrounds the fighting word

parts.note: to ford a river is to cross it
war is fighting

explanation.surface: Someone angry about fighting at the front of the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry; it is the verb to ford. 'The van' is the vanguard, the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The van is the leading position, so being in the van means being at the front.

clue.text: An animal in malice beheaded, it is used in the laboratory

definitions.text: it is used in the laboratory

indicators.note: in places the animal inside the shortened malice word
beheaded means the first letter is cut off the word for malice

parts.note: spite is malice
a pet is a domestic animal

explanation.surface: An animal kept out of spite is killed, and then used for experiments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' leaves PITE once the malice word loses its first letter; the definition is a whole descriptive phrase, as older puzzles often allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin glass tube for measuring liquids is standard laboratory equipment.

clue.text: Ballet for the sensible girls

definitions.meaning: a 1940 ballet by Frederick Ashton to music by Bach arranged by William Walton
the prudent maidens of the parable in Matthew's Gospel who kept oil for their lamps

explanation.surface: A dance work about prudent young women.
explanation.definitionFit: The parable of the ten maidens names the prudent five this way, and a ballet took the title.

clue.text: It sounds as if I give voice to something sweet

indicators.note: the phrase announces that the letters are what is heard, not what is written

parts.note: I sing, put as I followed by giving voice

explanation.surface: A singer claims to voice something sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar coating on a cake is a sweet thing.

clue.text: Go for a group

definitions.meaning: Scots and northern dialect verb meaning to go or walk
a band of people, such as criminals or workers

explanation.surface: Go off to join a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense is Scottish, as in Burns's 'gang aft agley'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect verb to walk, and a band of people working or acting together.

clue.text: Musical occasion for those who enjoy the pipes

definitions.text: Musical occasion for those who enjoy the pipes

parts.words: Musical occasion for those who enjoy the pipes
parts.note: pipes suggest musical instruments, but they are tobacco pipes: a Victorian concert where the men could light up

explanation.surface: A recital for lovers of pipe music.
explanation.walkthrough: A Victorian and Edwardian all-male evening of music where tobacco was allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: A men's musical evening at which tobacco was permitted, so pipe users enjoyed it.

clue.text: I enter a carriage fit for a king

indicators.note: enter means go into, so the letter I goes inside the carriage

parts.note: a pram is a baby carriage

explanation.surface: I climb into a coach worthy of royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: A pram is a baby carriage, not a royal coach.
explanation.definitionFit: The aged ruler of Troy in Homer's Iliad was a monarch.

clue.text: The lion Peter tangled with has plenty to eat

indicators.note: tangled means the letters of lion Peter are mixed up together

explanation.surface: A man named Peter wrestles a lion that has fed well.
explanation.definitionFit: Fullness from abundant food is the state that plenty to eat brings.

clue.text: An unoccupied vehicle goes to the top of the hill but it does not kill

parts.note: blank means empty, unoccupied
a cart is a simple vehicle
a ridge is the crest of a hill

explanation.surface: An empty wagon climbs a hill harmlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of the hill' looks like an instruction to take the first letter of 'hill'; it is a whole word, RIDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A round with powder but no bullet makes the bang without harming anyone.

clue.text: Lack of vigour of a state without women?

parts.note: a stag party is for men only
a nation is a state

explanation.surface: A country of men only has no energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Torpor or inactivity, the condition of something gone still and dull.

clue.text: Scholarly writer gets his study back

parts.note: Edward Lear, the nonsense poet

indicators.note: back means the study word is read in reverse order

parts.note: a den is a private study or room

explanation.surface: An academic author returns to his office.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone erudite and well read is scholarly, a synonym.

clue.text: To make a girl get into bed is the height of one's ambition

parts.note: Eve, a girl's name
to rest is to lie down in bed

explanation.surface: A man whose highest ambition is to bed a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The world's highest mountain is the classic figure for the ultimate goal.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest mountain on Earth stands for the ultimate goal anyone could aim at.

clue.text: Colour that is up and down as a source of comfort

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the pieces are read upward, in reverse

parts.note: red is a colour
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hue that rises and falls is consoling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RED plus IE into EIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A quilt stuffed with soft duck feathers gives warmth and comfort in bed.

clue.text: Something sweet may become Electra

indicators.note: may become signals the name Electra can turn into another word by rearranging

explanation.surface: The tragic heroine Electra might turn sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: Electra is the vengeful heroine of Greek tragedy, hardly sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Golden syrup or molasses is a sticky sweet substance.

clue.text: For creation I would be needed in addition to the lawgiver

indicators.text: would be needed in addition to
indicators.note: the letter I plus the answer together make the letters of creation

explanation.surface: God the lawgiver needed help to create the world.
explanation.walkthrough: Creation's letters are the answer plus I, so the answer added to I can be rearranged into creation.
explanation.definitionFit: One who enacts laws makes them, as a legislator does.

clue.text: Part of body given a poke on a wild occasion

parts.note: the shin is the front of the lower leg
a dig is a poke or jab

explanation.surface: Someone takes a jab in the leg at a rowdy party.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy, lively party is a riotous gathering.

clue.text: Place of the relative in Buddhist writing

indicators.note: in places the relative inside the Buddhist text

parts.note: a sutra is a Buddhist scripture
Ma is mother, a relative

explanation.surface: Where a relative appears in Buddhist scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: The large Indonesian island is a geographical location.

clue.text: Hop it as anagram turns into series of illusions

indicators.note: turns into signals the letters of hop it as anagram are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rude dismissal is rearranged into a dreamlike show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anagram' is part of the fodder here, not the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A shifting sequence of dreamlike images, as in a magic-lantern show, is a parade of illusions.

clue.text: Place which is among the reasons why they like holidays

indicators.note: among says the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A resort is among the reasons people enjoy their holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: HYTHE is a seaside town in Kent, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside town in Kent is a location.

clue.text: Not that it has to be after it for a tragic character

parts.words: it has to be after it for a tragic character
parts.note: add the word be after the answer to get the doomed lover of Pyramus

explanation.surface: Not that one: it must follow to make a tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The lover of Pyramus in Ovid, and in Shakespeare's play within A Midsummer Night's Dream, is THISBE: the answer with BE after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The near pronoun is the opposite of the far one, so it is the word chosen instead.

clue.text: African who needs a little drink after a hot number

indicators.note: after places the little drink behind the hot number

parts.note: taken as written
ten is a number
a tot is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: An African wants a nip after a sweltering spell.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is an old, now offensive name for the Khoikhoi people of southern Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated term for one of the Khoikhoi people of southern Africa.

clue.text: There is nothing in a chap returning with one for her

indicators.note: in places the nothing letter inside the reversed chap
returning means the chap word is read backwards

parts.note: a man is a chap
O looks like zero, nothing
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A girl joins a returning man who has nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns MAN into NAM; O goes inside, then I follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, the mother-in-law of Ruth in the Bible, so a female person.

clue.text: Strain tone badly, being loud of voice

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of strain tone are mixed up

explanation.surface: A singer strains the voice and shouts.
explanation.definitionFit: Stentor was a herald in the Iliad with a powerful voice, giving a word for booming.

clue.text: Before long a girl is without love

indicators.note: without means outside, so the girl's name goes around the love letter

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Soon a girl will be lonely without romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking; here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word meaning soon or shortly.
